key_insight: Uncertainty-guided, retention-constrained fine-tuning improves an aluminium MACE potential for defect dynamics while preserving tested bulk elastic and vibrational behavior.
engineering_relevance: The protocol supports more reliable atomistic simulations of aluminium plasticity without sacrificing near-equilibrium mechanical fidelity.
method: Acquire configurations using uncertainty from sensitivities over 144 readout weights, updating covariance within each batch.
Iteratively fine-tune all model parameters with relative-energy anchoring to retain historical behavior.
Gate updates against historical elastic-group energy and vibrational tolerances.
evidence_signal: After four rounds, 32 acquired configurations and 400 gradient updates, mean development force error fell from 22.43 to 21.52 meV/Å, outperforming sampling baselines; all three force-uncertainty runs met retention criteria, with harmonic phonon RMS drift below 0.05 THz.
watch_item: Retention is demonstrated only for the tested aluminium potential and evaluation conditions; broader deployment requires renewed validation and acceptance gating.
paper_title: Retention-constrained fine-tuning of a pre-trained aluminium MACE potential for non-equilibrium defect dynamics and plasticity
